title: Strict quotient reduction model and completion-unit normalization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $T$ a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived category [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the completion reflector $C_T$ with unit $\eta_T$ onto the full derived-complete subcategory of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]; thus $C_TV=R\lim_n(V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T)$. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use the small diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Its constant ring sheaf is $\Delta\underline A_T$ and its quotient ring sheaf is $B_T=(\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with the actual quotient transitions. A $B_T$-module system consists of module sheaves $M_n$ over $\underline{A_n}_T$ and $\underline{A_{n+1}}_T$-linear transition maps to $M_n$ by restriction of scalars. Write $\Delta$ for the constant-tower functor, $U_T$ for restriction to constant-$A$ towers, $S_T=-\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T$, $\mathcal R_T=S_T\Delta$, $i_V:\Delta V\to U_T\mathcal R_TV$ for the quotient augmentation, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ on constant-$A$ towers, with its canonical identification $\ell_V:\mathcal L_T\Delta V\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then: (1) the ring sheaf $B_T$ realizes the category of strict semilinear quotient systems, with componentwise kernels, cokernels and cohomology, and $U_T$ is exact and conservative on derived categories; (2) for every $V\in D_T$, a single flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to V$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives a K-flat diagonal $\Delta Q$ and represents $\mathcal R_TV$ by the strict complex $(Q\otimes_A\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with quotient transitions, and under this identification $i_V$ is represented by the termwise quotient maps; (3) the constant-tower functor $\Delta$ preserves K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and on a K-injective $V$ the map $\ell_V$ is represented by the literal equality $\lim\Delta V=V$; (4) $\mathcal L_TU_T\mathcal R_T=C_T$ canonically, and $\mathcal L_T(i_V)\ell_V^{-1}=\eta_{T,V}$. These are identities of natural transformations in $V$.

proof.text: Use the proved ordinary strict quotient presentation, which constructs its own normalized additive constant-ring sequence-module equivalence and proves diagonal flatness. It supplies the coefficient map, exact diagonal, insertion and reduction isomorphism without assuming a derived assertion.

Vertical evaluation is exact by its existing evaluation-topos API. Scalar restriction is exact and its derived functor reflects isomorphisms by the proved scalar-restriction API. Compose with the constant-ring tower equivalence and its induced derived equivalence to get exact and derived-conservative restriction.

Use the existing flat-term K-flat resolution for an arbitrary complex, and pass to any derived object using essential surjectivity of localization. The ordinary diagonal calculation makes its diagonal K-flat. The universal derived scalar-extension comparison is therefore invertible there; exact scalar restriction, the tower equivalence and ordinary reduction isomorphism preserve its invertibility.

Evaluation at level zero is exact and left adjoint to the constant-tower functor: a map into a constant tower is determined by its zero component, and the inverse correspondence precomposes with transition maps to level zero. The induced adjunction preserves K-injective complexes. The fully faithful constant/limit adjunction supplies a natural ordinary complex isomorphism, whose degree maps are the level-zero limit projections. Descend the ordinary constant-cone unit and the right-derived limit comparison through localization. It is invertible on K-injective complexes and therefore on all derived objects, using functorial K-injective resolutions. Its inverse is the required ell.

Whisker the exact diagonal factorization, universal scalar-extension comparison, exact restriction factorization, tower-equivalence factorization and ordinary reduction isomorphism into one natural comparison alpha. The universal quotient-tower presentation gives a canonical map from the composite reduction/restriction functor to the quotient presentation. On a flat-term K-flat representative both comparison maps are invertible, so this canonical map is an isomorphism on every derived object. Transport the left-derived universal property along it and lift the ordinary quotient augmentation to obtain i, with the representative equation. Whiskering the isomorphism with derived limit gives c. State both normalization laws as equalities of natural transformations; their component equations follow by evaluation. This avoids repeatedly expanding complex-composition conversions.

The inverse ordinary constant-limit isomorphism followed by the limit of the ordinary quotient augmentation has the defining projections of ordinaryUnit, hence equals it by uniqueness of a limit lift. Check the desired natural-transformation identity on a flat-term K-flat representative; these detect equality by essential surjectivity. Cancel the invertible derived-limit image of the quotient comparison. Substitute the representative formula for i and c and the formula for ell inverse. Naturality of the right-derived limit comparison reduces the equation to the just-proved ordinaryUnit equality and the quotient presentation unit law. This proves equality of the whole derived morphism, rather than only its projections.

theorem strictQuotientDiagonalNormalization [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    ∃ (d : StrictQuotientDiagonalPresentation J A I)
      (i : (constantTower J (constant J A)).mapDerivedCategory ⟶
        d.reductionD ⋙ d.restrictionD)
      (ell : (constantTower J (constant J A)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        rlim (constant J A) ≅ 𝟭 (D (constant J A)))
      (c : d.reductionD ⋙ d.restrictionD ⋙ rlim (constant J A) ≅ completion J A I false)
      (literalLimit : ∀ P : Cx (constant J A),
        (ordinaryLimit (constant J A)).obj
          (((constantTower J (constant J A)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≅ P),
      (∀ n : ℕ, PreservesFiniteLimits
        (SheafOfModules.systemSequenceEvaluation (finiteSystem J A I) n) ∧
        PreservesFiniteColimits
          (SheafOfModules.systemSequenceEvaluation (finiteSystem J A I) n)) ∧
      PreservesFiniteLimits d.restriction ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits d.restriction ∧
      (∀ {V W : D (strictQuotientRing J A I)} (f : V ⟶ W),
        IsIso (d.restrictionD.map f) → IsIso f) ∧
      (∀ P : Cx (constant J A),
        CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := constant J A) P →
        (∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := constant J A) (P.X q)) →
        (CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := strictDiagonalRing J A)
          ((d.diagonal.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ∧
          (∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite
            (J := WeilConjectures.coefficientSequenceTopology J)
            (R := strictDiagonalRing J A) (d.diagonal.obj (P.X q))) ∧
          IsIso (d.representative P) ∧
          i.app ((Q (constant J A)).obj P) ≫ d.representative P =
            (constantTower J (constant J A)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P ≫
              (TQ (constant J A)).map
                ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex (reductionUnit J A I false) (.up ℤ)).app P))) ∧
      (∀ V : D (constant J A), ∃ (P : Cx (constant J A))
        (_e : (Q (constant J A)).obj P ≅ V),
        CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := constant J A) P ∧
          (∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := constant J A) (P.X q))) ∧
      (∀ P : Cx (constant J A), P.IsKInjective →
        CochainComplex.IsKInjective
          (((constantTower J (constant J A)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)) ∧
      (∀ (P : Cx (constant J A)) (q : ℤ), (literalLimit P).hom.f q =
        limit.π ((constantTower J (constant J A)).obj (P.X q)) (op 0)) ∧
      (∀ P : Cx (constant J A), P.IsKInjective →
        (limitComparison (constant J A)).app
            (((constantTower J (constant J A)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
          (rlim (constant J A)).map
            ((constantTower J (constant J A)).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app P) ≫
          ell.hom.app ((Q (constant J A)).obj P) =
            (Q (constant J A)).map (literalLimit P).hom) ∧
      (∀ P : Cx (constant J A),
        CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := constant J A) P →
        (∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := constant J A) (P.X q)) →
        c.hom.app ((Q (constant J A)).obj P) ≫
          (rlim (constant J A)).map ((quotientPresentation J A I false).comparison.app P) =
            (rlim (constant J A)).map (d.representative P)) ∧
      ell.inv ≫ Functor.whiskerRight i (rlim (constant J A)) ≫ c.hom =
        completionUnit J A I false
